Former NSW deputy premier John Barilaro is re-entering politics after being hired by a federal Nationals senator.

Mr Barilaro led The Nationals in NSW until 2021, leaving parliament in that year before taking up a high-paying trade role in New York.

His appointment to the $500,000-a-year role was controversial but an inquiry into whether he engaged in corrupt conduct over the appointment was dropped.

Nationals frontbencher Ross Cadell on Thursday confirmed he hired Mr Barilaro to help with constituent and stakeholder engagement ahead of the next federal election.

First reported by Sky News, the move “to bring John into the team is about broadening the knowledge and reach of my office when it comes to regional communities and the people within them”, Senator Cadell said.

“John’s experience will be of great value as we develop policy and engage in the lead -up to the next election,” he said.

Mr Barilaro’s resignation from politics in October 2021 came days after then-NSW premier Gladys Berejiklian quit amid a corruption investigation.

He said at the time that his exit was motivated by personal reasons and not Ms Berejiklian’s resignation.

A probe into his subsequent trade appointment found one of his staffers inquired about the position a month before Mr Barilaro announced his resignation and a senior NSW public servant had been verbally offered the role a month before that.

The inquiry heard the offer to the public servant, Jenny West, was effectively rescinded and she was told after Mr Barilaro’s resignation that the job would be “a present for someone”.

A month later Ms West was made redundant from her role as Investment NSW deputy secretary.

Mr Barilaro was announced as New York trade commissioner in June 2022 only to quit two weeks later amid intense scrutiny over his appointment.

He always maintained he followed due process and the inquiry did not find he committed any misconduct.

Originally published as Nationals senator hires John Barilaro for part-time job
